description: Contract versioning lock. One row per PUBLIC contract: what it is, who owns it, which version is published, what its consumers are, and where its contract tests live. The architecture gate fails when a published contract's surface changes without its version changing. Intentionally tiny: this is not semver-as-a-framework, it is a change alarm.

breaking: removing or renaming an error code, or changing an existing code's HTTP status
changing the meaning or required shape of a request/response field
narrowing accepted input or widening required output
moving a file out of the declared public surface
patch: internal implementation changes with no surface change
policy.rule: A BREAKING change requires: major bump here, a note in docs/n8n-lego/BACKEND_LEGO.md §Contract changelog, and sign-off from every consumer listed below.
policy.preRelease: Contracts at 0.x are provisional: they may break with a minor bump, but the bump is still mandatory.

compatibilityModel.note: 0.x contracts are provisional: ^0.2.1 does NOT accept 0.3.0, because a 0.x minor is allowed to break. Consumers of a 0.x contract must be told about every minor.

policy.parentChildRule: A parent contract does NOT version-bump because a sub-LEGO changed compatibly. It bumps only when its own parent-facing surface moves. Example held by the fixtures: reference.validation 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 (additive) leaves reference.lego at 1.0.0 and reference.repository at 1.0.0. A BREAKING child change that surfaces through the parent does force a parent major bump.
policy.migrations: A contract may declare `migrations: ["1.3.0"]` — versions that need a data/state migration even though they are semver-compatible. Migration points are declared, never inferred.

contracts.notes: Read-only identity projection. Holds NO authority: no session creation, no password verification, no token minting. Introduced in P2.9 to retire allowances A1/A2. Adding an export is a contract change requiring a version decision; the surface is pinned by test/lego-boundary.test.mjs.

Fifteen public exports (scope 12.1; compat 13.1) + applyCompatibilityPolicy (15.2). MINOR 1.1.0 (P2.18): ENVELOPE_FIELDS gains optional 'causationId' — identifies the immediate parent request that caused this envelope (derived default = parent requestId). serialize/deserialize boundaries unchanged.

Four interaction classes with dispatch contracts and backpressure. MINOR 1.1.0 (P2.18): export BATCH_LIMITS (batch ceiling 256) and bound applyBackpressure — 'buffer' applies a declared onOverflow (or refuses with lego.backpressure) instead of queueing past highWaterMark; 'block' reports 'blocked' synchronously and offers bounded pushAsync waiting; highWaterMark validated as an integer in [1, 65536].

consumers: backend LEGOs that move an envelope + payload across any boundary (CALL/EVENT/STREAM/BATCH)
contracts.notes: Universal transport & envelope kernel (P2.18): deterministic canonical-JSON encode/decode of {envelope, payload}, fail-closed validation on entry (lego.contract_violation), declared KERNEL_LIMITS bounds (64 KiB message, 128-char ids, depth 32). No HTTP/broker/daemon — transport adapters arrive in P2.21.
Capability discovery and the lifecycle state machine. Nesting never grants access: reaching a nested LEGO requires an explicit declaration naming that child.

Provider-neutral AI vocabulary. CONTRACT ONLY: no inference, no agent loop, no gateway client, no MCP server or client, no network call, no new dependency. Vendor names appear only as examples of provider kinds, never in an id, a required field or a default.

P2.13 smallest additive publication from the already-declared ai.context fields and Context & Session operation vocabulary. The implementation is bounded local state only: no model/provider/runtime dependency, no transcript dump, no Memory store. Contract lock publication does not make P2.13 complete; Manager reconciliation, merge validation and post-merge verification remain required.

P2.13 smallest additive publication from the established ai.agent-session fields and states. A session is bounded identity/control state with references, never an unbounded transcript. The implementation remains provider/runtime-neutral.

Skill = procedural knowledge + rules + procedure + capability map + validators. The REGISTRY is implemented; skills stay declarative documents and nothing executes a procedure. FOUR published operations only. register/select/load/release are internal lifecycle methods of the registry object, deliberately NOT published caller operations: publishing load would make lazy discovery a caller concern, and publishing register would let a caller mutate the vocabulary other consumers negotiate against. There is no execute operation and no ai:skill:execute permission — execution is not a skill operation, so no published name may imply it. A skill DECLARES requiredCapabilities and never grants them; the capability system stays the sole authority. validate-selection checks the DECLARATION, never the caller's authorization. An unknown capability fails closed. Locked in P2.12 finalize by XA-19; XA-11 (whether Skill ultimately belongs under ai-foundation) remains open-for-manager and is a separate architecture decision that this lock does not settle.

P2.14 bounded Memory: persistent knowledge that survives context replacement. Four operations only: remember/recall/list/forget. Provider is the persistence boundary (InMemoryProvider default, replaceable). No vector search, no embedding, no model dependency. Integrity via sha256 canonical checksum, isolation by scope namespace, explicit forget semantics.

P2.15 bounded Workspace: identity, metadata, opaque resource references and logical lifecycle behind an explicit provider seam. No filesystem, terminal, process, credential, model, tool, MCP or runtime authority.

P2.16 bounded Agent Machine execution foundation (1.0.0) extended additively in 1.1.0: one canonical state machine for machine, agent and task identity, the canonical agent lifecycle plus the machine-level ready state, bounded step bookkeeping, first-class budgets (incl. maxChildren / maxTasksPerAgent), deterministic transitions, a replaceable provider/executor seam, bounded delegation edges with explicit narrowed grants (no permission inheritance), bounded execution graph representation/validation and Universal Agent Event derivation. It consumes ai.context, ai.agent-session, ai.memory and ai.workspace by opaque reference only and never redefines them. Nine operations and the five canonical ai:agent:* permissions; delegation is bookkeeping, never execution. No loop, no inference, no tools, no scheduler, no shell, no filesystem, no process. Waiting is fail-closed: approval resolution is the ai.approval contract's boundary, not this one.
changelog: 1.1.0 (P2.16): additive. Added agentId identity (distinct from machineId and taskId), capabilityScope (validated against the lego-foundation capability registry; unknown fail closed), bounded delegation edges (agentMachine.delegate + ai:agent:delegate — explicit narrowed grant, no permission inheritance, bounded budget and deadline clamped to the parent), the ready lifecycle state (agentMachine.prepare; created -> running stays legal, 1.0.0 flows unchanged), bounded execution graph representation/validation (validateAgentGraph: sequential, parallel, conditional, fan-out, fan-in, join, retry; cycles rejected), Universal Agent Event derivation (deriveAgentMachineEvents: agent.created/started/delegated/completed/failed/cancelled), maxChildren and maxTasksPerAgent budget bounds, and operation/permission fail-closed surfaces. The startedAt field the record always carried is now declared in fields. No 1.0.0 operation, state or transition changed meaning.

No storage engine, no filesystem authority, no download server — storage providers remain contract-only.

No executor of any kind.

P2.19 structured audit foundation (implementation: agent-1): fixed field set (auditId/eventType/timestamp/actor/subject/operation/result/correlationId/causationId/references/metadata), event types quoted from the canonical events.types vocabulary plus artifact.referenced (P2.19 acceptance), injectable clock and id factory, bounded capacity with deterministic drop-oldest retention, secret- and reasoning-shaped input refused fail-closed. In-process only — no production audit store, no unbounded append.

Declaration + seam + simulator only: no MCP, no model inference, no production scheduler, no shell/filesystem/subprocess authority — adapter selection grants nothing. contracts.notes: P2.22 node portability foundation (implementation: agent-1): language/runtime-neutral node contract — canonical portability classes (PURE/API/NETWORK/FILESYSTEM/NATIVE_PROCESS/ENVIRONMENT_SPECIFIC/REMOTE_BRIDGE), machine-readable runtime matrix (JS/WASM/RUST_NATIVE/REMOTE as SUPPORTED|UNSUPPORTED|CONDITIONAL with explicit conditions), language-neutral schema subset with SUPPORTED|UNSUPPORTED|LOSSY refusal (PORTABILITY_REFUSED, never silent coercion), five-axis compatibility report (contract/schema/runtime/portability/environment — never collapsed into one boolean), fail-closed reasons (unknown runtime/class/capability/permission, missing permission, environment/transport mismatch all refused), policy-based runtime selection (no language preference), declared-facet differential comparison. Classification only: portability grants no authority — permissions stay with the capability/approval system; no Node Creator, no translation engine, no provider integration, no model inference, no production distributed runtime.

contracts.notes: P2.23 node creator & translation foundation (implementation: agent-1): bounded definition producer — candidate/reference output only, zero standing authority (declaration ≠ authorization at every layer). One validation pipeline for human-created, node-created and translated candidates (origin is provenance, never a bypass). Deterministic offline translation: identical input ⇒ identical output and identical refusals; lossy/unknown source constructs REJECT with canonical reasons (schema issues reuse the P2.22 family verbatim — no second error vocabulary); credential-shaped source fields refuse the whole translation. Approval touchpoint = P2.19 foundation, policy-explicit (node-created OR authority-bearing class), fail-closed via evaluate(); artifact result = P2.19 registry reference (storageRef+checksum+metadata, content never dereferenced) produced only after granted approval — PUBLISHED_REFERENCE means publishable-by-a-system-with-authority, the creator holds none. Portability verdict comes from node.portability@1.0.0#canPort only. No publish op, no execute op, no grant op, no model, no network, no self-modification.

consumers: frontend read-only display of usage certainty (reported/estimated/unavailable, XA-17 current interpretation)
cost derivation via calculateCost — pricing basis handed by the caller, never fetched; missing pricing yields unavailable, never a guess
budget views over recorded usage — empty scope is unavailable, never a fabricated zero
contracts.notes: P2.24 token & usage honest accounting (implementation: agent-1): the ONE canonical usage publisher (XA-17 resolution — no second contract, no parallel vocabulary). Every figure carries value+kind+source+certainty; reported only when the source supplied the number, estimated only with a named deterministic estimator, unavailable as null (never 0, never exact). P2.13 token vocabulary quoted byte-for-byte (message/modelInput/output — no provider synonyms coined). Scopes are call/run/session per XA-17; requestId identity is idempotent (retry never double-counts, reuse with a different payload is refused). Cost = reported usage + known pricing basis + declared rule only; module ships no pricing, fetches nothing, bills nothing. Closed record shape refuses prompt/completion/credential fields; string identifiers are scanned for full credential shapes (detector matches canonical token shapes, not bare prefixes). Injected now/newId, zero imports, frozen records, bounded store (4096).

contracts.notes: P2.25 first real model provider adapter (implementation: agent-1): explicit configuration only (no discovery, no default provider, no default model), call-time authorization naming the published ai:model:* permission exactly (XA-8/XA-10 consumed unchanged; configuration is never authority — invoke requires an explicit grantReference), injected synchronous exchange edge with at most one attempt per call (no internal retry), canonical error translation (timeout->deadline_exceeded, down->unavailable, rate-limited->backpressure, forbidden->access_denied) with no raw provider body/key/prompt/completion echoed, bounded input/output/stream dimensions, stream usage finalized once at the final envelope (in-chunk usage cannot double-count), missing usage is unavailable (null, never 0) and only reported figures report into ai.token-usage@1.0.0 with requestId-derived identities (idempotent). Credentials are never stored: config refuses credential fields and credential-shaped values (full-form detector quoted from ai.token-usage). No-provider state is the canonical zeroInstall not-configured answer via describeProviderConfiguration(null). fail-closed on unknown model/tool/config/authorization; provider available never means invoke authorized.

consumers: consumers of the canonical tool contract — MCP and future gateways map ONTO this contract, never the reverse

contracts.notes: P2.25 first real tool provider adapter (implementation: agent-1): tool declaration / capability / permission / invocation / provider binding stay five separate concepts — a generic provider configuration is never execution authority. sideEffects is required and validated against the published vocabulary (unknown effects are treated as destructive and refused); requiresApproval tools demand an approval reference (presence enforced here, ai.approval decides the grant). tool.call is non-idempotent: one exchange, never retried internally, requestId required — replay with the same canonicalized payload returns the recorded outcome with no second exchange (results travel as opaque references, never stored for replay), a different payload under the same requestId is refused (request-id-reuse), and the requestId travels to the provider for its own dedupe. Reads are idempotent and also single-shot (maxAttemptsPerCall 1). Explicit configuration only, credentials never stored, canonical error translation with no echo, bounded lists/resources/prompts/results, no token figures invented (usage stays with the model side per ai.token-usage). fail-closed on unknown tool/config/authorization/provider responses.
